title: Temporal export grants and PII-aware field masking for usage analytics exports
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams need to export granular usage records for billing reconciliation, security investigations, and legal requests. Current export endpoints return wide records and rely on client-side filtering, which risks accidental exposure of PII (user identifiers, email addresses, API keys) and lacks time-limited access control. Exports are also heavy on pipeline resources when large historical ranges are requested.

Proposal: Implement a server-side, RBAC-aware export mechanism with two core pieces: (1) Ephemeral Export Grants — short-lived, auditable tokens scoped to a specific export request (datasets, date range, fields allowed, and purpose). Grants are created via an admin API and require permission checks; they expire automatically and can be revoked. (2) Field Mask Engine — a policy-driven transformation layer in the analytics pipeline that applies per-field redaction/masking, conditional on the requestor's roles, grant scope, and customer entitlements. The Field Mask Engine supports allow-lists, hash-pseudonymization, and full redaction for sensitive fields.

Design notes and constraints:
- Grants are first-class objects in the console backend (export_grants table) and audited for compliance. Grant creation must require an admin or a documented approval workflow when the scope includes sensitive fields.
- Export tokens must be bearer tokens with short TTL (default 30 minutes, configurable by policy) and stored hashed in the DB for introspection.
- The Field Mask Engine should execute as a pluggable transform in the usage pipeline (pre-export step) and should be performant for large batches; prefer streaming, row-by-row transforms rather than loading entire export blobs into memory.
- Provide two export modes: (A) Masked Export (default) — PII masked according to policy; (B) Full Export (restricted) — available only when grant explicitly allows and when security_review_required is satisfied.
- Audit trail: every export request must emit an export_audit event with grant id, user id, IP, dataset rows count estimate, and link to resulting artifact (S3 path). These events are retained per compliance retention policy.
- UI/Console: Add an "Export with masking" dialog for workspace admins with fields for dataset, time window, field selector (with sensitivity tags), and purpose. Show required approvals for Full Export.
- Backwards compatibility: Existing export endpoints remain but will be rate-limited and deprecated in favor of the new grant-based flow. Document migration path for support teams.

Trade-offs considered:
- Implementing masking in the pipeline vs. precomputed masked materialized views. We prefer pipeline transforms to avoid storage duplication and keep policy logic centralized, at the cost of CPU at export time. If export load proves high, we can add periodic masked snapshots.
- Per-field encryption at rest was rejected for this ticket due to key management complexity; instead we rely on masking/pseudonymization and strict access controls.

Acceptance criteria:
- An admin can create an export grant scoped to a workspace and field-set via API/UI.
- An export request using a valid grant returns an S3 artifact with fields masked as per policy; full export is gated and only possible with explicit grant flags and security review state.
- All export actions produce audit events and entries in export_grants.audit_log.
- Performance: Exports for 10M rows with typical field masks complete within target SLA (TBD, initial target 30 minutes) and do not cause pipeline instability.

Migration steps and rollback:
- Feature-gate via console-2025.03 flag; route 20% of small exports to new pipeline for monitoring. If errors exceed threshold or latency regressions observed, rollback gating at API gateway.
